Psalm 2
Status
Approved
Script
Ever feel like the whole world is spinning out of control?
Psalm 2 opens right there. Nations raging. Rulers plotting to break free from God and his chosen King. The New Testament tells us David wrote it.
And heaven? God isn't worried. He laughs. Then he speaks: "I have set my King on my holy hill."
Here's the key. The word for God's "Anointed" is the Hebrew mashiach. Messiah. In Greek, that's Christos. Christ. And when God tells his King, "You are my Son," the New Testament applies those very words to Jesus.
So the chaos is real, but it isn't in charge. And the psalm ends the way Psalm 1 began, with the word "blessed." Blessed are all who take refuge in him.
Next time the news feels loud, take it to the King. The world rages. Jesus reigns.
Review notes
Author: Acts 4:25–26. Nations and rulers: 2:1–3. God laughs, King on Zion: 2:4–6. Anointed: mashiach in 2:2, rendered christos in the Greek Old Testament and quoted in Acts 4:26. "You are my Son": 2:7, applied to Jesus in Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5, echoed at his baptism (Mark 1:11). Bookend: "Blessed" opens Psalm 1:1 and closes Psalm 2:12.
Voiceover
ElevenLabs, Max – Warm Captivating Narrator, speed 1.00, stability 50%, similarity 75%. Hebrew spelled mah-SHEE-akh for the narrator. Final audio 54.4 seconds; video 56.1 seconds.
